question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Hermann Tertsch (PfE), Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE), Jorge Martín Frías (PfE) Subject:

On 16 April 2026, coinciding with the visit of the Spanish Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, to China, the Second Deputy Prime Minister of Spain, Yolanda Díaz, responded to a question on whether human rights were respected in China by stating that the Asian country was ‘making gradual progress and strengthening the rule of law’1. It is worth remembering that one month earlier, on 12 March, Xi Jinping’s regime passed the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, which strengthens the policies of systemic repression of ethnic, cultural and religious minorities that have been implemented by Beijing for years, in particular in the regions of Xinjiang, Tibet and Inner Mongolia, as well as against Christian churches, which are subjected to a programme of forced Sinicisation conducted by the Communist Party2. In view of this: Does the Vice-President / High Representative agree with the Spanish Government’s view, expressed by its Second Deputy Prime Minister, that the rule of law is being strengthened in China?

https://www.ondacero.es/noticias/espana/yolanda-diaz-reconoce-que-china-regimen-pluripartidista-pero-queavanza-estado-derecho-actor-clave-mundo_2026041669e097729e87c91dbff67f9f.html. https://persecution.org/2026/03/16/chinas-ethnic-unity-law-deepens-repression-of-minorities/.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.6.2026) The EU’s position on the human rights and rule of law situation in China is well known and has been set out in its public statements and in its exchanges with the Chinese authorities, including in the framework of the EU-China Human Rights Dialogue1 and in statements at the UN Human Rights Council2. The EU has consistently expressed its concerns about the human rights situation in China and has repeatedly urged China to abide by its obligations under national and international law, to respect, protect and fulfil human rights for all, and to uphold the rule of law. These concerns include the situation in Xinjiang, Tibetan areas and Hong Kong, as well as the situation of human rights defenders, lawyers and journalists. The EU has also repeatedly called on China to respect the rights of persons belonging to ethnic, religious and linguistic minorities, including their right to freely enjoy and preserve their culture, religion or belief, language and identity. The EU will continue to engage with China on human rights and the rule of law, both bilaterally and in multilateral fora, while reiterating its long-standing position that respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms, due process and the rule of law are essential elements of EUChina relations.
